title: Your first Java program
summary: What every line of Main.java does, then run it.

steps.title: Open Main.java
steps.say: Every Java program starts somewhere. Press **Ctrl+P**, type `Main` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

steps.title: Find it
steps.say: It may be further down. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `public class Main` and press Enter to jump to it.

waitFor.hint: find public class Main with Ctrl+F.

steps.title: The class
steps.say: `public class Main` is the **class**: a container for code. The file's name matches it (`Main.java`). Everything else goes between its `{` and the last `}`.

steps.title: Find it
steps.say: It may be further down. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `public static void main` and press Enter to jump to it.

waitFor.hint: find public static void main with Ctrl+F.

steps.title: Where it starts
steps.say: `main` is the method Java runs first. Copy this line exactly in every program for now; you'll learn what each word means in the Methods lesson.

steps.title: Find it
steps.say: It may be further down. Press **Ctrl+F**, type `System.out.println` and press Enter to jump to it.

steps.title: Printing
steps.say: `System.out.println(...)` prints a line of text. The text in double quotes is a **String**, printed exactly as written. The `;` ends the statement.

marks.label: a String: text in double quotes

steps.title: Run it
steps.say: Click the **Run** button (▷) at the top right of the file. The output appears in the terminal at the bottom.

waitFor.hint: run the program and read the output.

steps.title: Check your work
steps.say: When it runs the way you expect, open the lesson chip and press **Verify**. Each checkpoint tells you what it's looking for if it doesn't pass yet.
